rules.name: R1. Simple probing on an equation (family simple_probing; milestone M1)
rules.condition: Row r of row_list::simple_probing is live, row_lower == row_upper == b finite with |b| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility, and row_free_size[r] >= 3 (two free entries are a doubleton equation and stay with doubleton_t). After refresh_activity neither activity has an infinite term (min_act.inf_count[r] == 0 and max_act.inf_count[r] == 0), so every free column has finite bounds. Quick test in O(1): |(M - b) - (b - m)| less both error bounds is at most tol.feasibility, m and M being the compensated minimum and maximum activity. Then one scan of the row looks for the binary p: a free integer column with col_upper - col_lower == 1 exactly for which both conditional rows are forcing in the engine's own sense: gap_low = (b - m) - |a_p| and gap_high = (M - b) - |a_p| each pass the test of forcing_row (E/src/rules_rows.cpp:152-180) evaluated on the free entries other than p: |gap| + error <= tol.feasibility * min|a_i| / max(1, max|a_i|), and when one of those columns is continuous the gap may be positive only by rounding (the error bound plus forcing_rounding_units rounding units of the terms). Smallest column index among several (in exact arithmetic at most one column can qualify when the row has three or more free entries, because the ranges of the other columns add up to |a_p|). Every other free column i has u_i - l_i <= alias_scale_limit = 1e6 (a named constant and a function of the state, so a second presolve skips the same rows). Effect: delete_row(r); every other free column i gets x_i = v_low_i + (v_high_i - v_low_i) * (x_p - l_p), where v_high_i is the bound the row forces on i when x_p = l_p + 1 (for a_p > 0 the minimum-activity bound of i: l_i if a_i > 0, else u_i) and v_low_i its other bound; a_p < 0 exchanges the two. The bounds are read before the first substitution. Applied in full with the substitution code shared with the doubleton family, with no budget test inside the row and no bound transfer (the image of the two values of p is exactly the two bounds of i).
rules.validity: Class B/S, primal: the alias holds at every feasible point; on in primal-only mode. Proof: the term of p takes one of two values that differ by |a_p|. With the larger one the rest of the row must equal its minimum activity plus gap_low, with the smaller one its maximum activity minus gap_high; both gaps are zero within the forcing tolerance, so each other column sits at the bound named above. Floating point: this is the conclusion the engine already draws for a forcing row, with the same tolerance and the same restriction to rounding-size gaps when a continuous column is in the row (a real gap g leaves such a column g/|a_i| off its bound, and another row that holds it with a larger coefficient would be violated by more; rules_rows.cpp:140-151). I take this test and not the absolute 1e-9 of HiGHS (H/presolve/HPresolve.cpp:2696-2698, read) that worth_first and engine_fit copied: an absolute gap of 1e-9 is not small for a column with |a_i| = 1e-6. An integer column gets an integral scale and offset because its bounds are integral, which the stack contract asks (E/include/gprs/postsolve.hpp:77-81). Activities are over explicit bounds only (HiGHS also reads implied bounds); a row that balances only through an implied bound of a continuous column fires in the rounds after make_explicit.
rules.postsolve: Existing alias record with the new field origin = probing and row = r. Undo x_i = scale * x_p + offset as today. Crush: nothing; p stays and every feasible point satisfies the alias. The deleted equation leaves no record: with the aliases composed it is a constant, which the rows test of the structure check covers as it is.
rules.cost: O(1) per listed row for the quick test, where most rows end; one row scan for the binary; then the live entries of the substituted columns and of p, spent on the family's budget {4, 2, 1e5}. The stop is tested between two rows; a row whose columns do not fit the remaining budget goes back on the list. A column is substituted once, so the total over the presolve is at most the nonzeros. Called once per round, after the doubleton equations. The list gets every activity, activity_unread, side and entries event of a row, so nothing is left to history and the family never reports limited.
rules.worth: Measured (G/results/bench240/cheap_ablation/off_simple_probing.csv, recomputed in abl.out): without it HiGHS keeps 1.0103 times the nonzeros, 1.0106 the rows and 1.0220 the columns in the geometric mean over 237 instances; 8 instances change: highschool1-aigio 3.04, neos-1445765 1.96, brazil3 1.86, the two cryptanalysis instances 1.009, academictimetablesmall 1.007. Counters (reader): 296,239 substitutions on 13 instances, 98% on the first three. Predicted gate after it: about 0.968 (0.9563 today).

rules.name: R2. Free singleton column with an equation as pivot row (family column_rules; M2)
rules.condition: Column k is live with csc.size[k] == 1; its entry a lies in the live row r with row_lower == row_upper == b finite and row_free_size[r] >= 2. b' = b less the terms of the fixed columns, |b'| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility. Implied free by r alone on explicit bounds, in O(1) from the stored activities: with rest_min and rest_max the activity of r without the term of k, the ends low = (b' - rest_max)/a and high = (b' - rest_min)/a (exchanged for a < 0), each moved outward by candidate_slack (E/src/rules_propagation.cpp:140-152), must satisfy: col_lower[k] == -inf or low >= col_lower[k] - implied_tolerance, and col_upper[k] == +inf or high <= col_upper[k] + implied_tolerance, with implied_tolerance(bound) = 2 * (4 * rounding_unit * |bound| + tol.activity_error_share * tol.feasibility), which is what two candidates of one bound can differ by (the lower limit of improvement_step, rules_propagation.cpp:57-67). An end whose residual has an infinite term fails unless the bound of k on that side is infinite. The error guard of bound propagation applies, with one fresh summation when it drops an end. Integer k: every other free column of r is integer, every a_i/a is integral within tol.zero with a * round(a_i/a) equal to a_i within tol.zero, and b'/a is integral within tol.zero with |a * round(b'/a) - b'| <= tol.feasibility (the test the alias forest makes for an edge between integers, postsolve.hpp:160-165); otherwise the column is left and nothing is concluded. With a finite bound of k: max|a_i| / |a| <= pivot_ratio_limit = 1000 (named constant). q = cost[k]/a and every new cost are finite. Effect as one transaction: save the row; delete_row(r); set_cost(i, cost_i - q * a_i) for every saved entry with the cancellation rule of substitute() (rules_doubleton.cpp:148-157); add_objective_offset(q, b'); set_cost(k, 0); remove_col(k). No row gains an entry.
rules.validity: Class S, primal; on in primal-only mode. At every feasible point x_k = (b' - g)/a, g being the saved entries, so the cost moves exactly and crush is dropping k with equal objective. The end test is the range of (b' - g)/a over the explicit bounds of the other columns, so the restored value is inside the bounds of k (to the tolerance) for every point inside the bounds of the reduced model, not only for feasible ones; k is in no other row, so the row carries nothing else. One implied premise, the pivot row itself, recomputed at application. No recorded implied bound is read: a record depends on the order of visits and on the 1e-3 step (rules_propagation.cpp:168-188) and a second presolve builds it differently. After make_explicit the explicit bound of a singleton column is the candidate of its only row moved outward, so the test still passes and a second presolve decides the same. The test of b'/a for an integer singleton, which PaPILO's SingletonCols lacks by the reader's report, is part of the condition; 2x + 2y = 3 with an integer singleton x is a fixed oracle case.
rules.postsolve: New record col_from_rows {col, n_rows = 1, first_row, col_lower = -inf, col_upper = +inf, prefer = 0} with one saved row {row r, coefficient a, lower = upper = b', the free entries of r other than k}. Fixed terms are folded into b' as read_edge does (rules_doubleton.cpp:42-68), so a saved row names only columns that are live at the push. Undo: x_k = (b' - compensated sum of the saved entries at the restored values)/a, rounded to the nearest integer for an integer column; not clamped (the row stays exact, the bound holds to the tolerance). Crush: k is dropped.
rules.cost: O(1) to accept or reject on the stored activities; a firing costs the row once (save and cost move), for an integer column one more scan. The objective gains up to len(r) - 1 nonzero costs, reported as the statistic cost_fill. Saved entries count against options_t::saved_row_factor (4) times the input nonzeros; at that limit the family reports limited.
rules.worth: Measured for HiGHS rule 8, equation and inequality pivots together (off_rule8.csv): 1.0089 nonzeros, 1.0026 rows, 44 instances: mcsched 1.63, swath1 and swath3 1.245, neos-3627168-kasai 1.226, neos-3046615-murg 1.127, blp-ar98 1.098, irish-electricity 1.090, supportcase7 1.071, leo1 1.063. Counters (reader): 16,881 firings on 59 instances, the most widespread cheap rule; one firing removes a whole row. The counters do not split the two pivot kinds; M2 measures R5 by its own switch.

rules.name: R3. Zero-cost singleton column (family column_rules; M2)
rules.condition: Column k is live, continuous, csc.size[k] == 1, cost[k] == 0 exactly; its row r has two finite sides (an equation included) and row_free_size[r] >= 2; R2 did not take it. With a the coefficient: L' = L - max(a*l_k, a*u_k) and U' = U - min(a*l_k, a*u_k), a new side being infinite where the bound it needs is infinite. Skipped when a needed finite bound gives an infinite term (is_infinite_term) or a finite new side v has |v| * tol.side_error > tol.feasibility. Effect: save the row; delete_entry of (r, k); set_row_lower(L') and set_row_upper(U'), or delete_row when both are infinite; remove_col(k). A one-sided row is not this rule's: there the column has no lock in one direction, and the lock rule (finite bound) or R4 (infinite bound) owns it, as in HiGHS (H/presolve/HPresolveZeroCostSingleton.cpp:15-31, read). Not taken for an integer column (the set of rest values would have holes).
rules.validity: Exact projection: the values g of the other columns for which some x_k in [l_k, u_k] satisfies L <= a*x_k + g <= U are exactly L' <= g <= U' (the column is continuous, so the union of the shifted intervals is one interval). The cost is zero, so every feasible point crushes by dropping k with the same objective, and every reduced point extends. No lock, activity or optimality argument is used, so no error bound enters; each new side is one compensated difference (shifted_side, E/src/state_ops.cpp:155-161) under the side guard. Mode: the plan puts singleton-column rules in class D and switches D off in primal-only mode (PLAN/DESIGN.md:437, 630-632), although the rule keeps the sentence of options_t::primal_only (E/include/gprs/presolve.hpp:83-85). It is off in primal-only mode by one test inside the family until the owner decides (decision 2).
rules.postsolve: col_from_rows {col k, one saved row with the original sides L and U less the fixed terms and the free entries other than k, col_lower = l_k, col_upper = u_k, prefer = l_k if finite, else u_k if finite, else 0}. Undo: the interval that the bounds and the saved row allow for x_k at the restored values; x_k is its point nearest to prefer; when rounding makes it empty, the point of [l_k, u_k] nearest to the row's interval. Deterministic, no search. Crush: k is dropped.
rules.cost: O(1) test; a firing costs the row once. The row stays in the model, so repeated removals from one long row are what saved_row_factor bounds.
rules.worth: Measured (off_rule18.csv): 1.0012 nonzeros and 1.0064 columns, 16 instances: timtab1 1.098, neos-4954672-berkel 1.086, icir97_tension 1.055 (columns 1.77), pg 1.020, supportcase12 1.012. Counters: 58,511 firings on 19 instances, 55,681 on supportcase12. It is one of the rules on the path to neos-3402294-bobin (132 firings there; see R4).

rules.name: R4. Forcing column (family column_rules; M2)
rules.condition: Column k is live, of any type and length, cost[k] == 0 exactly, and either down_locks[k] == 0 with col_lower[k] == -inf and up_locks[k] >= 1, or the mirror. This is exactly the case the lock rule leaves today (E/src/rules_dual_fixing.cpp:49-55; rules.hpp:309-310 says 'Stage 3 removes it with its rows'). Effect: every live row of k is saved without k and deleted, then remove_col(k). When the used slots of its rows do not fit the remaining budget the column goes back on the list.
rules.validity: Lock argument with zero cost; an exact projection. No down lock means that every row of k is one-sided in the way that lowering x_k never hurts (a ranged row or an equation would lock both ways), and the bound below is infinite: for any values of the other columns a value of x_k satisfies all its rows and its upper bound, so these rows restrict nothing else, and the objective does not see x_k. Lock counts do not depend on bounds or activities (state_ops.cpp:88-99), so no tolerance enters the premise; the cost test is exact zero as in the lock rule (HiGHS allows a small tolerance by the reader's report). An integer column is rounded further into the free direction, which keeps every saved row satisfied. Class L by the plan: off in primal-only mode until decision 2.
rules.postsolve: col_from_rows with all rows of k (each with its coefficient, its sides less the fixed terms and its free entries other than k), col_lower, col_upper, prefer = the finite bound, or 0 when both are infinite. Undo: the interval that all saved rows and the bounds allow, its finite end rounded inward for an integer column, then the point nearest to prefer; in the down-free case this is min(u_k, min over the rows of (side - g_i)/a_i), floored for an integer. Crush: k is dropped.
rules.cost: O(1) test; a firing costs the entries of the rows of k once. Those rows leave the model, so the saved entries of this rule are bounded by the nonzeros.
rules.worth: Measured (off_rule7.csv): 1.0001 nonzeros and 1.0005 rows on three instances (neos-2746589-doon 1.027 in nonzeros and 1.124 in rows, neos-3656078-kumeu 1.006, neos-3402454-bohle in columns only). Counters: 381 columns and 2,856 rows on 5 instances. neos-3402294-bobin, the largest gain of the set (ratio 0.19; 0.0070 of the 0.0447 mean log gap) has the same 381,000 nonzeros in all thirteen ablation files. Its all-cheap run shows (bobin.py, from highs_cheap_all/summary.json) 132 forcing columns that remove 132 rows, so they are singleton columns, 132 zero-cost singletons, then 1,848 fixings counted as weakly dominated and 556,248 redundant rows, while the lock rule fixes nothing on the input. The chain is therefore R3 and R4, then the lock rule the engine has. That it carries over to the engine is inferred, not run; M2 tests it.

rules.name: R5. Free singleton column with an inequality as pivot row (family column_rules; M2; the first new dual rule)
rules.condition: Not in primal-only mode. Column k is live with csc.size[k] == 1 and cost[k] != 0; its row r is no equation. The tight side S is the side of r that k is pushed against when it moves to lower cost: the activity then moves in the direction -sign(cost) * sign(a); downward takes row_lower, upward row_upper; S must be finite (when it is infinite the column has no lock in its cost direction and the lock rule owns it). Then every test of R2 with b' = S less the fixed terms: both ends of (S' - rest)/a against the bounds of k within implied_tolerance (an infinite bound needs nothing), the integrality conditions for an integer k, the side guard and pivot_ratio_limit. Effect as R2: the row is deleted and the cost moves onto its other columns.
rules.validity: Class D, an exchange that moves only the removed column; off in primal-only mode. From a feasible point move x_k in its cost direction until r is tight at S: x_k' = (S' - g)/a. No other row holds k; the bound in the direction of the move is implied by the end test; the bound behind it is not passed because the move goes away from it; the cost falls by |cost| times the distance; for an integer k the value is integral by the conditions. So an optimal point has r tight, and the reduced model is the original restricted to that. The second end test is not needed for this exchange; it makes the restored value keep the far bound for every point of the reduced model. validity_first and worth_first asked for an infinite far bound instead; that is the special case, and engine_fit's two-end form is the one taken. It is the plan's pivot row 'weakly dual-implied with the pivot column as source' (PLAN/DESIGN.md:469-470) and the case HiGHS reaches in the cheap setting (H/presolve/HPresolve.cpp:2457-2485, read; that the implied dual bound of the row is cost/a is the reader's inference). A row whose dual sign is known only through another column is not taken, because no row-dual state is built.
rules.postsolve: col_from_rows as in R2 with lower = upper = S'. Undo x_k = (S' - sum)/a. Crush: k is dropped; the reduced objective of the crushed point is the objective of the moved point, so it is not above that of the point. The finding counts in dual_findings.
rules.worth: Part of the 1.0089 of rule 8; M2 measures its share by switching it alone. With R2 to R4 this is the largest milestone in the prediction: gate about 0.968 -> 0.985, of which bobin is 0.007.

rules.name: R6. Parallel columns: fixing by dominance (family parallel_cols; M3)
rules.condition: Not in primal-only mode. Detection: per live column a key (number of live entries; hash over row and coefficient divided by the coefficient in the smallest row index), recomputed for columns whose entries changed. A bucket is the set of columns with equal key in index order. A singleton column has its row as key, so all singleton columns of one row form one bucket, as in HiGHS (H/presolve/HPresolveParallelRowsAndCols.cpp:38-40, 75-76, read). Exact test of a pair p < q: the same live rows and one ratio s = a_q/a_p with |a_q - s*a_p| <= tol.zero * |a_q| in every row and |a_q - s*a_p| * R <= tol.activity_error_share * tol.feasibility, R being the largest finite |bound| of the column that is fixed (tol.feasibility/tol.side_error when one is infinite). D = cost_q - s * cost_p as a compensated value; the costs count as equal when |D| <= tol.cancellation * (|cost_q| + |s * cost_p|). Moving delta from q to p (x_q - delta, x_p + s * delta) changes no row and changes the cost by -delta * D. Cases in this order: (a) D >= 0 or equal: q is fixed at its finite lower bound when p can absorb s * (x_q - l_q); (b) D <= 0 or equal: q is fixed at its finite upper bound when p can absorb in the other direction; (c) and (d): the same with the roles exchanged (ratio 1/s). 'Can absorb in a direction': the bound of the absorber in that direction is infinite, or one of its rows implies it: the candidate of that row over the explicit bounds of its other columns (O(1) from the stored activities, moved outward by candidate_slack) is within implied_tolerance of the bound; the rows of the absorber are scanned and the first that implies is taken. Types: an integer absorber needs an integer moved column and an integral factor (s or 1/s within tol.zero); a continuous absorber takes a moved column of either type; a continuous column is never moved onto an integer. An infinite target bound is left alone (no status is concluded). One pair at a time, every premise computed at application. A bucket of singleton columns is scanned as a group when a member is listed: one pass finds the absorbers (the implied test of a singleton column reads only its row); without an absorber nothing more is done and nothing is left undone; with absorbers every other member is tested against them in index order, at most opt.parallel_bucket_limit absorbers per member, beyond which the call reports limited.
rules.validity: Class D, an exchange with a recorded compensation; off in primal-only mode. For a feasible point move the fixed column to its bound and the absorber by the factor. Every row keeps its activity. The absorber stays inside its bound: the bound is infinite, or it follows from one row and the explicit bounds of that row's other columns, and after the move that row still holds and every other column, the fixed one included, is inside its explicit bounds. One implied premise, tested weakly, which is enough because the bound stays in the model and nothing is dropped on its strength. The cost does not rise by the sign of D; integrality holds by the type rule. HiGHS has the same four cases with the weak implied test for a MIP (HPresolveParallelRowsAndCols.cpp:143-157, 249-286, read) and accepts |D| up to its dual tolerance; here the sign of D is exact apart from the cancellation tolerance, so that 'not above' in the checks needs no exception. Rejected: engine_fit's form with a plain fixed-column record and crush promising nothing, which no solver-free check could test where the rule fires; and engine_fit's exclusion of singleton columns (PaPILO skips them, ParallelColDetection.hpp:204-205, read on the node): on neos-3004026-krka, satellites2-60-fs and satellites2-40 every column this rule fixes in HiGHS is a singleton (6,435, 820 and 600 fixings with as many entries) and on rail01 and rail02 most are (par.out).
rules.postsolve: New record parallel_fix {col, value, kept, ratio}, written by a helper next to fix_column (E/src/rules_bounds.cpp). Undo: x[col] = value. Crush, at the record's position in the replay: w[kept] += ratio * (w[col] - value), then col is dropped. The record exists so that the default-mode crush check and the oracle test this rule on feasible points: a wrong implied test puts the absorber outside its bound, a wrong sign raises the objective.
rules.cost: Keys: the entries of the columns whose entries changed. Comparisons: a listed column against at most opt.parallel_bucket_limit neighbours above and below in its bucket, each the column length; a scan that ends on the limit with columns left reports limited, as the parallel rows do (E/include/gprs/rules.hpp:228-233). Absorb test: one scan of the absorber with O(1) per row. A parallel pair that is left alone marks both columns; only while marks exist does the family expand its row list to the marked columns of the listed rows, otherwise it drops that list. Budget {8, 8, 1e5}, once per round. HiGHS's column loop costs 2.3 s on the 240 instances (reader).
rules.worth: Measured for dominance and merge together (off_parallel_columns.csv): 1.0104 nonzeros, 1.0139 columns, 39 instances. By the counters dominance carries about 85% of it (par.out: 2.09 of the 2.45 summed log): nw04 1.92, decomp2 1.53, neos-3004026-krka 1.26, neos-2987310-joes 1.23, rail02 1.10, swath1 and swath3 1.09, n3div36, co-100, neos-5093327-huahum and irp 1.05 to 1.06. 103,066 fixings on 24 instances. Predicted gate after it about 0.994, the first value above 0.99.

rules.name: R7. Dual bound strengthening (family column_rules; M4)
rules.condition: Not in primal-only mode. Column j is live with down_locks >= 1 and up_locks >= 1 (a column without a lock in one direction is the lock rule's, which stays first and unchanged in the cascade). Direction down when cost >= 0 (a new upper bound), up when cost <= 0; with cost == 0 down first and up only when down changed nothing. Down: for every live entry (i, a) of j that locks it down (a > 0 with finite row_lower, a < 0 with finite row_upper), w_i = (side - rest)/a, rest being the activity of row i without the term of j at the end that works against that side (the minimum for the lower side, the maximum for the upper side), O(1) from the stored activities. The attempt ends without a result at the first row whose rest has an infinite term, whose side fails the side guard, or whose error bound fails the guard of bound propagation after one fresh summation. w_i is moved upward by candidate_slack; for an integer j it becomes ceil(w_i - tol.feasibility / max(1, |a|)). u' = max(col_lower, max_i w_i). Taken when u' < col_upper - tol.feasibility and |u'| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility. u' == col_lower: fix_column(j, col_lower). Otherwise an integer j gets tighten_upper(u') and a dual_bound record; a continuous j is fixed only when every w_i <= col_lower + tol.feasibility / max(1, |a|) and is otherwise left, so that explicit bounds of continuous columns stay what section 6 of the plan says they are. Up is the mirror.
rules.validity: Class D, an exchange that moves only column j; off in primal-only mode. For a feasible point with x_j > u' set x_j = u'. Every row that locks j down holds at u' whatever the other columns do inside their explicit bounds, by the definition of w_i; every other row only gains from a decrease; the cost does not rise; an integer stays integral. An equation among the rows gives a w_i that is at least the bound the equation implies, so the clip never acts through it. The activities are the engine's compensated sums with their error bound, every rounding goes to the safe side (a larger bound), and the integer rounding divides the tolerance by |a| as HiGHS does (the readers cite H/presolve/HPresolve.cpp:4442-4454), so the row is violated by at most the tolerance at the rounded bound; PaPILO's absolute 1e-9 on plain sums is not copied. Explicit bounds only; HiGHS reads implied bounds here, which the rounds after make_explicit give. The plan's guard 'dual arguments use continuous columns only' concerns columns that supply row-dual bounds; this rule uses none.
rules.postsolve: A fixing leaves the existing fixed_col record (crush drops the column, which is the move). A tightening leaves the new record dual_bound {col, bound, is_upper}: the primal postsolve ignores it, and crush clips w[col] to the bound at that position of the replay.
rules.cost: One scan of the column with O(1) per row, ending at the first row that gives no bound, with no allocation. A column is tested at most once per call and the family is called once per round, not inside the cascade, where worth_first had put this rule. That is part of the rule: HiGHS reruns its dual-fixing extensions after every change and pays 144 of its 302 seconds for it (157.3 s with rule 17 off; rd-rplusc-21 takes 106.4 s against 0.63 s while the extensions fire zero times; abl.out). markChangedCol walks the whole column while any single-equation flag is set (H/presolve/HPresolve.cpp:621-628, read).
rules.worth: Measured for the three dual-fixing extensions together (off_rule17.csv, the same table as off_dual_fixing_substitution.csv): 1.0063 nonzeros, 1.0080 rows, 1.0076 columns, 40 instances: supportcase12 1.755, radiationm40-10-02 1.333, radiationm18-12-05 1.316, var-smallemery-m6j6 1.163, neos859080 1.067, rocII-5-11 1.052. By the counters this rule carries supportcase12 (184,311 fixings) and, with R8, the radiation instances: 205,092 fixings on 26 instances and 19,965 bound changes on 39.

rules.name: R8. Alias of a single-lock column to a binary of its lock row (family column_rules; M4). HiGHS's dual-fixing substitution and the port of cuOpt's single_lock_dual_aggregation in one rule
rules.condition: Not in primal-only mode. Column x is live with finite bounds l < u, u - l <= alias_scale_limit, and either cost >= 0 with down_locks == 1 (case down) or cost <= 0 with up_locks == 1 (case up; down first when both hold). The lock row r is found by one scan of the column; r is no equation and has at most options_t::lock_alias_row_limit = 1000 free entries (HiGHS's cap, H/presolve/HPresolveDualFixing.cpp:36-38). Case down, the locking side of r being its lower side for a_x > 0 and its upper side for a_x < 0: for each free binary p of r (integer, bounds exactly 0 and 1, p != x) in increasing column index, and for v = 0 then v = 1: (i) release: with the term of p set to a_p * v the locking side holds for every value of the other columns, x included, by the redundancy test of the row rules on the stored activities (tolerance less the error bound); (ii) force: with p at 1 - v the bound of x implied by the locking side reaches u, for a continuous x within tol.feasibility / max(1, largest |a| of column x), for an integer x after round_lower_integer. Both are O(1) per binary. The first hit gives x = l + (u - l) * p for v = 0 and x = u - (u - l) * p for v = 1; case up is the mirror. Applied with the shared substitution code; r stays in the model.
rules.validity: Class D, an exchange that moves only the removed column; off in primal-only mode. With p = 1 - v every feasible point has x = u (a bound fact, to a tolerance scaled by the largest coefficient of x so that no other row of x moves by more than the tolerance). With p = v move x to l: the locking side of r holds by (i); the other side of r, if finite, only gains from a decrease; no other row locks x down; the cost does not rise. So an optimal point satisfies the alias, and the reduced model is the original with that equation added, so every reduced point is a point of the original. Only the locking side has to be released. HiGHS (HPresolveDualFixing.cpp:72-80, read) and cuOpt (single_lock_dual_aggregation.cpp:383-400, read) test every finite side, which is stricter than the proof needs, and engine_fit and worth_first followed them. The force test reads the lock row only, as cuOpt does; HiGHS's implication over all rows that the two columns share (:82-90) is the extension if M4 measures a gap. cuOpt's rule (a binary x, the lock row, both polarities; :171-186, 308-369) is the special case u - l = 1; HiGHS's substitution is the case v = 0. An equation as lock row is not taken: it locks both ways and belongs to the single-equation extension, which is not built.
rules.postsolve: Existing alias record with origin lock and row = r. Undo as for any alias. Crush: x is dropped, which is the exchange. The finding counts in dual_findings. The structure check passes any such alias inside its bounds and asserts that none exists in a primal-only result; whether it keeps an optimal point is tested by the oracle and by the crush of feasible points.
rules.cost: O(1) prefilter (one lock, finite bounds, cost sign); then one scan of column x for the lock row and its largest coefficient, one scan of r of at most 1000 entries, and the substitution (the entries of x and of p). Once per round for a listed column, after R7.
rules.worth: Part of the 1.0063 above. Counters (reader): 74,920 substitutions on 37 instances (physiciansched6-2 17,435, gfd-schedulen180f7d50m30k18 16,399, physiciansched3-3 15,598, radiationm40-10-02 8,425); the instances where only the substitution fires include var-smallemery-m6j6 1.163 and neos859080 1.067. Predicted gate after R7 and R8: about 0.9996. G/baseline/HIGHS_DIAG.md:828 records that in a full HiGHS presolve var-smallemery-m6j6 ends larger with this rule on; to be looked at again when the aggregator exists.

rules.name: R9. Parallel columns: merge (family parallel_cols; M5)
rules.condition: A parallel pair as in R6 whose costs are equal (|D| within the cancellation tolerance, in both modes) and to which no case of R6 applies; in primal-only mode R6 is off and the pair comes straight here. sigma = a_removed / a_kept. Two continuous columns: kept = the smaller index. Two integer columns: kept = the one for which sigma is integral within tol.zero (the smaller coefficients; the smaller index when |sigma| = 1), and |sigma| <= u_kept - l_kept + 1. One integer and one continuous column: the continuous one is kept and u_kept - l_kept >= |sigma| (or infinite), so no column changes type. Merged bounds l_kept + min(sigma*l_rem, sigma*u_rem) and u_kept + max(sigma*l_rem, sigma*u_rem), infinite where a needed bound is; a finite result passes the side guard. Effect: delete_entry for every entry of the removed column, set_cost(removed, 0), remove_col(removed), then set_col_lower / set_col_upper of the kept column to the merged bounds. In a bucket of singleton columns the members are sorted by cost/coefficient (the index as last key) and neighbours with equal ratio are tested.
rules.validity: Class S, primal; on in primal-only mode. z = x_kept + sigma * x_removed has the same row terms and, with equal costs, the same objective as the pair; every z inside the merged bounds splits into two admissible values: the interval sum for continuous columns, the HiGHS no-hole condition for two integers (H/presolve/HPresolveParallelRowsAndCols.cpp:316-322, read), and for a continuous kept column the intervals of consecutive integer values touch when its range is at least |sigma| (HiGHS's condition :298-307 with the roles exchanged: HiGHS keeps the integer and turns it continuous, which our state cannot do, col_type being written only at construction by the engine reader's report). Row activities do not change, because the range of the pair's term equals the range of the merged term, so bounds that other columns got from those rows stay true. Every row of the kept column loses an entry and so changes version (E/src/state_ops.cpp:499, read), which voids every implied-bound record taken from those rows, the kept column's own included, and set_col_lower / set_col_upper accept a wider bound (state_ops.cpp:260-276, read). So the merge needs no new state operation: worth_first's replace_col_bounds with an epoch and engine_fit's reset_implied are not needed. Costs agree to 1e-12 relative and not to HiGHS's dual tolerance, so that the objective identity of the checks holds.
rules.postsolve: New record merge {kept, removed, scale, kept_lower, kept_upper, removed_lower, removed_upper}; types from postsolve_t::col_type. From here on the kept index means z. Crush: w[kept] += scale * w[removed]. Undo in closed form without a search (HiGHS's fallback of up to 1000 unit steps is not copied): the admissible values of x_removed are its bounds intersected with those that leave z - scale * x_removed inside the kept bounds; x_removed is the admissible value nearest to its lower bound if finite, else to its upper bound if finite, else to 0, rounded into the admissible interval for an integer; x_kept = z - scale * x_removed. The conditions make the admissible set non-empty.
rules.cost: One column scan per merge; detection is shared with R6.
rules.worth: About 15% of the 1.0104 of parallel columns (0.36 of the 2.45 summed log, par.out): neos-4722843-widden 1.091 (12,950 merges), supportcase12 1.089 (5,701), mik-250-20-75-4 1.034, unitcal_7 1.026, fiball 1.017, rail507 and fast0507 1.013. 24,233 merges on 19 instances. final.state_and_driver:
All paths under E. Nothing here changes a Stage 1 result; the groundwork milestone proves that with the hashes.

1. No dual state. The state gets no row-dual bounds and no reduced-cost bounds, because no built rule reads them. Every premise of R1 to R9 is local to a column and its rows and is read from explicit bounds, sides, entries, lock counts, costs, types and the stored activities. 'A bound is implied' always means the candidate of one named row, recomputed in O(1) at application; a recorded implied bound is never read (rules_propagation.cpp:168-188: records depend on the order of visits and the 1e-3 step).

2. Lists and events (include/gprs/state.hpp, src/state_ops.cpp, src/state_build.cpp, src/hash.cpp).
- frontier_set_t::pending becomes uint16_t and the event masks and list_bit with it. Read: it is uint8_t today (state.hpp:110) with seven row lists in use (state.hpp:157-166).
- New row lists: simple_probing = 7, column_rules = 8, parallel_cols = 9 (count 10). row_event::activity, activity_unread, side and entries feed all three. At construction every row is on simple_probing and no row is on the other two, because every column starts on its own list.
- New column lists: column_rules = 2, parallel_cols = 3 (count 4), every column on both at construction. col_event::locks (pushed by set_cost, delete_row, change_side_locks, set_coefficient, delete_entry, move_entry; state_ops.cpp:229, 325, 363, 478, 501, 522, 539) feeds dual_fixing, column_rules and parallel_cols: each of these is a change of the cost, the locks or the entries of the column. New col_event::entries = column_rules | parallel_cols, pushed by scale_row for every live column of its row; read: scale_row changes every coefficient and pushes no column event today (state_ops.cpp:430-458).
- A bound change of a column gets no column event and needs none: set_col_bound pushes a row event for every live row of the column (state_ops.cpp:195-215, read), and the families expand listed rows to their columns. This keeps the hot path of set_col_bound as it is; engine_fit's col_event::bound is not taken.
- No type change, no relaxed bound on a column that keeps its meaning, no column version, no watch lists. The only bounds that widen are those of the kept column of a merge, whose rows all change version in the same step (R9).

3. Shared internal code that leaves anonymous namespaces, moved without change of behaviour: src/implied.hpp with candidate() (returning false where it asserts today), candidate_slack(), implied_tolerance() and the residual of a row without one column (from rules_propagation.cpp:97-152); src/alias_apply.hpp with substitute() and set_root_slots() taking an origin (from rules_doubleton.cpp:108-160); src/saved_row.hpp with the snapshot of the free entries and fixed terms of a row (as read_edge, rules_doubleton.cpp:42-68); src/parallel_keys.hpp with the hash, key and bucket code of the parallel rows, parameterised by the line store; the forcing test of rules_rows.cpp:152-180 as a function on a set of entries.

4. Records (include/gprs/postsolve.hpp, src/postsolve.cpp). alias_record_t gets origin {doubleton, probing, lock}. New kinds after row_addition, each arriving with its rule: col_from_rows {col, n_rows, first_row, col_lower, col_upper, prefer} with a pool of saved rows {row, coefficient, lower, upper, begin, end} and pooled entries (R2 to R5); parallel_fix {col, value, kept, ratio} (R6); dual_bound {col, bound, is_upper} (R7); merge {kept, removed, scale, four bounds} (R9). Stack contract: a saved row names only columns that are live when it is pushed and not the record's own column, which gives the invariant of DESIGN.md section 8 because a later merge of two saved columns is undone before the record that reads them; col_from_rows, parallel_fix and merge remove one column each; merge keeps the kept index with a new meaning; dual_bound removes nothing. postsolve() undoes the new column kinds in reverse order and ignores dual_bound. crush() becomes a forward replay on a copy of the point: parallel_fix moves weight, dual_bound clips, merge adds, every other record does nothing; then the kept columns are read. O(columns + records); on a Stage 1 stack it is the present restriction. postsolve_hash and stack_consistent name every new kind and field.

5. Families and options (include/gprs/rules.hpp, presolve.hpp, src/presolve.cpp; new src/rules_simple_probing.cpp, rules_columns.cpp, rules_parallel_cols.cpp). rule::simple_probing = 6, column_rules = 7, parallel_cols = 8, count = 9, each with its entry in enabled, budget ({4, 2, 1e5}, {8, 4, 1e5}, {8, 8, 1e5}) and statistics, so that work, seconds and findings are booked per family. options_t gets one switch per sub-rule (free_singleton, zero_cost_singleton, forcing_column, free_singleton_dual, dual_bound, lock_alias, parallel_dominance, parallel_merge), saved_row_factor = 4 and lock_alias_row_limit = 1000; result_t gets a finding counter per sub-rule and dual_findings, the number of reductions that keep an optimal point only (lock fixings, R5, R6, R7, R8). Primal-only mode: all three families are called; the dual sub-rules, and R3 and R4 until decision 2, test opt.primal_only themselves; dual_fixing stays off by rule index as today (presolve.cpp:153-156).
- simple_probing_t takes its row list (R1).
- column_rules_t takes its column list and its row list; its candidates are the listed live columns and the live columns of the listed live rows, each once per call, in index order. Per candidate: a singleton column tries R2, R3, R5; then R4; then, with locks both ways, R7 and R8. A candidate that a rule removes ends there. The stop is tested between two columns; unvisited columns go back on the column list.
- parallel_cols_t takes its column list (keys of these columns are recomputed) and, only while a left-alone mark exists, its row list, from which it lists the marked columns of the listed rows; R6 then R9 for every listed column with a bucket neighbour.
- Round (presolve.cpp:265-288): cascade, parallel rows, doubleton equations as today, then simple probing, column rules, parallel columns, each followed by end_phase(). The lock rule stays in the cascade and so runs before the column rules of the same state. The new phases come after the Stage 1 phases so that the first round does on the input model what Stage 1 does: the engine is ahead of the reference on nine instances through the row addition, which reads singleton columns that R2 and R5 remove. The families run in the rounds before and after make_explicit.
- pending(rule) maps each family to its lists; fixed_terms_matter() (presolve.cpp:293-297) and the renewed test after absorb_fixed_terms (:354) include the three families, which read sides and activities; phase_hash gets six entries per round.

6. Work over the whole presolve. Each family has a per-call budget, and each is called at most once per round; max_rounds = 20 counts the rounds of the whole presolve (presolve.hpp:96-97, presolve.cpp:262-269, read). So a column is tested by R7 and R8 at most 20 times and the work of a family is at most 20 times its call budget, without a cap that depends on history. Work and seconds per family are reported per instance at every milestone; a further cap is decision 6.

7. Fixed-point claim. result_t::fixed_point is the present expression (presolve.cpp:357-358) and additionally requires that none of the three families is waiting. With the flag set a second presolve finds nothing for R1 to R9 either. It rests on three things. (a) Every test reads the state as it is, never a record or the history of a row. (b) Every premise has an event: cost, locks and entries of a column through the column events, scale_row included; sides, entries and both activities of a row, and through them the bounds of every column of the row and the fixing of a neighbour, through the row lists. (c) The caps that stop a rule are functions of the state (alias_scale_limit, pivot_ratio_limit, lock_alias_row_limit, the first-hit order by column index), so a second presolve applies the same; the three that depend on history report limited: comparisons of a column that end on parallel_bucket_limit, more absorbers in a singleton bucket than that limit, and the saved-row limit. A call that stops on its budget returns its lists, as every family does. The implied tests allow two candidate roundings, so they give the same answer before and after make_explicit turned that candidate into the bound. Not covered, as today: the last bits of a stored activity. The three tests that run a second presolve (tests/test_engine_fixed_point.cpp, test_e2e_presolve.cpp:789-848, test_e2e_planted.cpp:287, by the engine reader) are the test of this paragraph, and the campaign tool gets a second presolve on a sample (it has none today, tools/gprs_fuzz.cpp:279-294, read).

8. Determinism. No hash container; buckets are sorted keys; candidates are processed in index order; ties go to the smaller column index (the binary of R1, the partner of R8, the kept column of R9, the absorber of R6). New lists and arrays enter state_hash.

9. Other places that write the six families out and follow (engine reader, the first read by me): tools/gprs_fuzz.cpp:216-222 (the shift r + 6 becomes r + rule::count; variants draw the sub-rule switches), tests/test_e2e_presolve.cpp:130-131, tests/test_engine_presolve.cpp:112, check/make_mutants.py:134-139 (text of active()), tests/test_hash_values.cpp.
final.checks:
Principle (from validity_first): every built rule has a forward map. For the primal rules crush keeps the point; for the dual rules the replay performs the exchange (R6 by its record, R7 by the clip, R5 and R8 and every dual fixing by dropping the column). So for any feasible point x of the original model the crushed point is feasible in the reduced model and its objective is not above that of x, in default mode too, and equal when result.dual_findings == 0. With the postsolve contract this proves that the optimum is kept, and both halves can be tested without a solver on any known point. Each check extension arrives in the same milestone as the rule it reads, with wrong engines in check/make_mutants.py that the named check must catch; a wrong engine that is not caught stops the milestone.

Groundwork (M0), before any rule and verified on Stage 1 results first. The four places that assume the lock rule is the only dual rule change together: tests/oracle.cpp:1005-1007 (read: today the crush test is skipped whenever the lock rule has a finding); the argument of check/crush_check.hpp:20-38, rewritten as an induction over the records with the replay; the verdicts of check/gprs_check.cpp:394-401 and of its cost variants; the stated reason of tests/test_e2e_planted.cpp:267-291. The structure-check extension for row_addition records, which exists outside the tree (HISTORY.md:1530-1541), is merged into stage1-v4 first, and an unknown record kind becomes an error instead of being read as a parallel row (check/structure_check.hpp:192-199, read).

Oracle and generator (tests/oracle.hpp, oracle.cpp).
- Crush test for every result that carries a model: with options.primal_only or result.dual_findings == 0 the crushed point is feasible with equal objective, otherwise feasible with an objective not above. The existing verdicts stay (outcome, optimum, postsolved optimal point, sampled feasible and far points) and remain the exact test of the dual rules.
- New knobs, all 0 by default so that old seeds give old cases: p_probing_row (an equation whose side is the midpoint of its activity range with a binary carrying half the range; variants off by one unit, with a range-2 integer in place of the binary, with a continuous column); p_forcing_col (a zero-cost line column with one infinite bound and one-sided rows); integer and zero-cost variants of p_singleton_col; p_parallel_col (a scaled copy of an earlier column with its own cost and bounds: integer copies of enumerated columns with scale 1, -1, 2 or -2, an enumerated copy of a line column, a line-column copy of a line column, and two singleton columns in one row); p_single_lock (a bounded column with one lock from a row that one value of a binary makes redundant, random cost sign). Profiles --columns, --parallel-cols and --single-lock in tools/gprs_fuzz.cpp next to --singletons.
- Class extension for twins only (from worth_first): a row may hold two line columns when they are a parallel pair. The solver splits: for each finite bound of either twin it fixes that column there and solves the rest, which is inside the class, and takes the best case. This is exact because for a fixed sum the objective is linear in one twin over an interval, so an optimum has one of the two at a bound; at least one twin has finite bounds. At most two pairs per model.
- Fixed cases: 2x + 2y = 3 with an integer singleton x (R2 must leave it); an integer singleton in an inequality with a fractional tight value; a zero-cost singleton in an equation and in a ranged row; an integer forcing column with fractional row limits; a probing row whose gap is just above the forcing tolerance; a merge with a negative ratio; two integers with ratio 2 and range 1 (a hole); a parallel pair whose absorber bound is implied by a set-partitioning row.
- Not exact: R2, R3 and R5 with a second continuous column in the pivot row (two unrelated line columns in one row are outside the class). The rules read the type of a neighbour only in the integrality test; these cases are covered by the planted-point test, the structure check and the real instances.

Structure check (check/structure_check.hpp), by milestone.
- M0: new test 'objective': the original objective composed through the records equals the reduced cost vector plus offset, coefficient by coefficient within the tolerance, with a zero coefficient on every variable that is not a reduced column. The file reads no cost today. It already tests the cost move of the doubleton substitution.
- M2, col_from_rows: column_map_t becomes a sparse linear form over check variables; a column removed by a col_from_rows record with an interval (R3, R4) is a virtual check variable with the box of its record. A saved row is the snapshot of its row at the push: each original row is tested against its first snapshot, each snapshot against the next snapshot of the same row, the last against the reduced row or, when the row left, over the bounds, all by the existing kept-rows test (implied_maximum, lines 235-280). R2 and R5: the box test of the form against the original bounds of the column, which is exact because the proof used the pivot row alone; the pivot row composes to a constant inside its sides; an integer column has an integral form. R3: the check recomputes the widened sides from the record and tests 'rest inside the widened sides' against the next snapshot or the reduced row, which is the existence of the undo value. R4: every saved row bounds the column from one and the same side and the column's bound on the other side is infinite, which is the existence proof. The paragraph at lines 41-52 ('no rule relaxes a bound ...') is rewritten.
- M3: parallel_fix is read as a fixed column (value inside the original bounds, integral for an integer) and must be absent from a primal-only result.
- M4: dual_bound must lie inside the original bounds; it and an alias of origin lock must be absent from a primal-only result.
- M5, merge: the reduced bounds of the kept column lie inside the sum of the two recorded ranges; the split domain is never empty (no-hole conditions recomputed from the record); the removed column enters every row as a parameter inside its recorded bounds with the coefficient a_removed - scale * a_kept, which must compose to zero; a row where it does not and that fails over the parameter's box is counted as merge_unproven and must be explained; the split is implemented a second time in the check and compared with postsolve() at both ends and the middle of the merged range.
- What the structure check cannot prove: that a parallel_fix had its absorber bound implied, that a dual_bound saw every locking row, that a lock alias had its row released. Those are the crush check's and the oracle's.

Crush check (check/crush_check.hpp) and real instances (check/gprs_check.cpp). Clauses 2 to 4 are verdicts in default mode for every rule, with the replay. If the owner switches R3 and R4 on in primal-only mode, their columns are excepted in the same way. A third mode is run next to default and primal-only: the dual sub-rules off and the lock rule on, so that a failure is attributed. Pushed points (push_point) stay. risks: The ablation measures what HiGHS loses without a rule, not what our form of the rule gains. The oracle campaign of each milestone is their first test. R5's two-end form and R8's locking-side release go beyond what HiGHS and cuOpt do.

The forward crush is new engine code and three checks lean on it. A crush error and a rule error look alike on a point that is not optimal; unit tests of crush alone and the wrong engines cr_replay and pd_crush are there for that. A future dual rule whose exchange moves a kept column must bring a record for it, as parallel_fix does, or the default-mode crush check reports false failures.

Each round expands the listed rows to their columns for column_rules, and for parallel_cols while a mark exists, and tests every listed column with locks both ways by one column scan; this is of the order of one or two propagation sweeps per round. The instances where HiGHS's extensions are slow (rd-rplusc-21 with 622 columns of 1,370 entries, neos-3402454-bohle, neos-4647030-tutaki) are the ones to watch. Memory. One saved row per removed singleton column: supportcase12 has 55,681 zero-cost singletons. A long row with many such columns is bounded only by saved_row_factor, which ends the rule with limited.

The engine is ahead of the reference on nine instances through the row addition. The new phases run after the Stage 1 phases, but from the second round on singleton columns may be gone before the parallel rows see them. The per-instance lower bound against v4pre catches this; the remedy would be an order change, not a rule change.

Numerics of substitutions. If the campaign shows such rows, the dynamism veto of the parallel rows belongs into the shared substitution code. The implied tests allow about 2e-7, and with a pivot ratio up to 1000 a restored singleton value can pass its bound by more than 1e-6 at a reduced point that itself uses the tolerance.

R3 turns equations into ranged rows, which the doubleton rule and the later aggregator cannot use as pivot rows; R9 turns two binaries into an integer of range 2; HIGHS_DIAG.md:828 records that the dual-fixing substitution makes a full HiGHS presolve end larger on var-smallemery-m6j6. decisions_for_owner: Rule list. Amendment A8 names dominated and weakly dominated columns by the bound on the reduced cost, implied equations, column stuffing, implied-integer conversion and the dual-fixing extensions as a whole for Stage 1c. All three designers and I leave the first four and the single-equation part of the fifth out of the required set: together they are about 1.0007 in HiGHS's own ablation, none has a forward map the crush check can test, and without them the engine needs no row-dual state. They are the optional milestone M6, built only on evidence. This changes A8 and needs your yes. Recommended: accept.

Primal-only mode for the zero-cost singleton (R3) and the forcing column (R4). Both are exact projections and keep the sentence of options_t::primal_only (every feasible point crushes to a feasible point with the same objective); the plan (DESIGN.md sections 4 and 8) puts them in the classes that are off there. I keep them off, as the plan says. Two designers would switch them on; that is one test per rule plus an exception in the round-trip clause of the crush check (z equals x) for their columns, the same kind of exception the merge needs for its pairs anyway. Worth in that mode: columns 1.0064 for R3.

Scope. The smallest set that passes 0.99 in the prediction is M1 to M3 (about 0.994 in nonzeros, six instances below 0.95 that only the missing rules explain). Recommended: M1 to M5 (about 1.00, nothing below 0.95, a margin of about one family for the weaker forms).

Merging two binaries or integers into one general integer (rail507, fast0507, fiball: about 1.3% each). HiGHS does it and the gate rewards it; PaPILO switches parallel columns off for pure binary models (read on the node). A merged column is no binary for the later clique and probing stages. I merge in Stage 1c and propose to look again when cliques exist; the alternative is to leave binary pairs with equal cost unmerged now.

Order of the new phases in a round: after the Stage 1 phases (chosen, to keep the first round and the engine's lead on nine instances as they are), or the singleton-column rules before the parallel rows (closer to HiGHS, where two thirds of the gain lands in the first scan).

Work over the whole presolve. Every family has a per-call budget and is called at most once per round, so max_rounds = 20 bounds its total work; I add no cap that depends on history (validity_first proposed 16 tests per column, worth_first 64 passes per family, both of which clear the fixed-point flag when hit). Say if a total cap per family is wanted in addition; work and seconds per family are reported per instance either way. Our own time target (summed engine time at most 1.3 times Stage 1's, no instance above twice its Stage 1 time plus 0.05 s) is a proposal next to your time rule.

BHW coefficient reduction is named for Stage 1c in A8 and A6 but is a row rule of the tightening family, has no counterpart in the reference and so no number against this gate. engine_fit builds it with the dual-fixing extensions; I put it after the gate (M6). Decide whether it is built inside Stage 1c.

Tolerances stricter than the reference, chosen so that the checks need no exception: exact zero cost in R3 and R4 (HiGHS allows a small tolerance for the forcing column), costs equal to 1e-12 relative for a merge and an exact sign of the cost difference in dominance (HiGHS: dual tolerance 1e-7), the engine's forcing-row test in simple probing (HiGHS and PaPILO: absolute 1e-9). They can be loosened one at a time after the gate shows what they cost.

Single-lock alias: the force test reads the lock row only (cuOpt's proof, generalised to any bounded column and both polarities; one rule then covers HiGHS's dual-fixing substitution and the A6 port of single_lock_dual_aggregation), and HiGHS's implication over all shared rows is added only if M4 measures a gap. Agreed, or HiGHS's form from the start?

Oracle. The exact oracle is extended by one case, parallel pairs of continuous columns (a split on the bounds of the pair), so that R6 and R9 on continuous pairs are tested exactly; rows with two unrelated continuous columns stay outside it and are tested by planted points. The alternative is no extension at all (validity_first).

PaPILO-only stronger forms are not built: removing a singleton column with a cost when only one bound is implied (the row stays, the objective gets denser) and dual bound strengthening of continuous columns (a bound from a cost argument on a continuous column is neither an input bound nor a row's candidate). They are beyond the reference; decide after the gate whether one is to be measured.
max_rounds stays at 20 until M2 reports the rounds; raising it is a default change that needs your word if instances end on it.
The reference for the 40 testbed instances has to be run with the switch set of highs_cheap_all, the nine instances above 1e7 nonzeros included; this is node time in M0.

What holds. I re-derived R1 to R9 against the engine sources (state_ops.cpp, rules_rows.cpp, rules_propagation.cpp, rules_doubleton.cpp, rules_dual_fixing.cpp, postsolve.cpp) and HiGHS (HPresolve.cpp 2400-2760, 3700-3840, 4380-4480; HPresolveParallelRowsAndCols.cpp 100-420; HPresolveDualFixing.cpp; HPresolveZeroCostSingleton.cpp) and found no model on which a stated condition holds and the reduction loses the optimum or relaxes the model in exact arithmetic. The reasons: every 'implied' premise is the candidate of one row over explicit bounds that stay in the model, so the circular use of a bound that the same row gave is harmless; the only bounds that widen are those of a merged column, and the undo splits inside the recorded boxes; the replay order of crush is the record order, and each exchange is argued on the model at that step. The two points where the design goes beyond its sources are right: R8 needs only the locking side released (cuOpt tests both sides at single_lock_dual_aggregation.cpp:386-400, HiGHS at HPresolveDualFixing.cpp:72-80; moving the column away from its only lock can only help the other side), and R5's two-end test is what keeps the restored value inside the far bound at every reduced point. Primal-only mode: R1, R2 and R9 keep the sentence of options_t::primal_only; R3 and R4 are exact projections, as the design says.

What is wrong. Nine defects: one rule condition that drops cases the lock rule does not own (R7 and the driver gate, a loss of reductions, not of validity); one missing size guard that gives postsolved points off by 5e-5 and more on allowed input (R6); a structure-check extension that was specified against a check file one version behind the tree and fails on correct results where row addition fired; an oracle extension that is not exact and can pass a wrong engine; and five smaller points (wrong engines that cannot be caught as named, chains of pivot ratios, the row of an R8 alias, the merge undo outside the bounds, clause 5 of the crush check).

defects.what: The structure-check extension (M0, M2, M5) is specified against the older check file. The design cites 'an unknown record kind is read as a parallel row' at structure_check.hpp:192-199 and implied_maximum at lines 235-280; those are the lines of the 483-line file in G/check. The file in E has 1062 lines, already reads row_addition records (compose_records :292-304, row_equations_t :387-436, the added_rows test :830-935; HISTORY.md Entry 31, lines 1836-1876, says it was merged into stage1-v4), and the design says nothing about how that test meets the new records.
defects.why_it_fails: R3 and R4 make their column a 'virtual check variable with the box of its record' and prove rows by a snapshot chain 'with the existing kept-rows test'. A row that had an equation subtracted is proved today from the reduced row of that equation (E/check/structure_check.hpp:843), a parallel-removed row from the reduced row of its kept row (:795-803). After R3 that reduced row is the widened one without the column, and the tie between the removed column and the rest is gone. Smallest model: E: x1 + x2 + x3 = 3; T: x1 + x2 + x3 + s <= 5; x1, x2, x3 continuous in [0,3], zero cost, in no other row; s >= 0. Row addition gives T': s <= 2 (a record), T' becomes a bound, and x1, x2, x3 are now singleton columns of E, which is what a subtraction leaves ('a column that only the two rows held becomes a singleton column', E/include/gprs/rules.hpp:288-290). R2 does not take x1 (3 - x2 - x3 reaches -3), so R3 removes x1 (E becomes 0 <= x2 + x3 <= 3) and then x2. The result is right: the undo restores x1 + x2 + x3 = 3 and T holds. The check as designed tests T = x1 + x2 + x3 + s with x1 and x2 free in [0,3], against E's reduced row or over the bounds: maximum 3 + 3 + 0 + 2 = 8 > 5, a failure on a correct result. The same happens to a row removed as parallel to a row that R3 widens later, and 'each original row against its first snapshot' picks the wrong snapshot when the kept row had one before the parallel record. Rows parallel up to singleton columns are where row addition fires (brazil3, piperout-d27, dlr2 with 202,759 subtractions) and their equations are where R2, R3 and R6 will fire, so M2's criterion 'structure check clean on the 240' cannot be met as specified; if such rows are counted as not tested instead, the rule runs unchecked there, which is the case of Entry 25.
defects.fix: Redo the check design on E/check/structure_check.hpp before M2. A snapshot must be usable as the 'reduced row' of an equation in the added_rows proof and of the kept row in the parallel-row proof, with the record's own column as a variable of that proof (the undo makes the snapshot hold, which the existence test proves), and the snapshot to use is the first one pushed after the row_addition or parallel_row record in stack order. R2 and R5 need nothing more: their pivot row composes to a constant. Add the model above as a test of the check and a wrong engine for the combination (R3 with a wrong side on the equation of a subtracted row). Drop 'merge the row_addition extension' from M0 (done); keep 'an unknown record kind is an error' (the else branch at :292 reads every other kind as a row addition).

defects.what: R6 fixes the dominated column at any finite bound; there is no size guard on that value. R3, R7 and R9 have the side guard (|v| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility); R6 uses the size of the bound only in the proportionality test, which exactly proportional columns pass with any bound.
defects.why_it_fails: The fixing is valid only together with the compensation, so the absorber ends at the same magnitude and the rows hold only to the spacing of doubles there. Smallest model: min x_p + x_q; row x_p + x_q + y = 3.7; x_p >= 0 without upper bound; x_q in [-1e12, 10]; y in [0,1] with a second row of its own. One ratio, equal costs (D = 0), absorber bound infinite: case (a) fixes x_q = -1e12. The reduced row is x_p + y = 3.7 + 1e12, which a double holds as 1000000000003.69995 (spacing 1.2e-4 at 1e12, checked with a one-line script); every postsolved point has activity 3.69995 in the original equation, 4.9e-5 off against a tolerance of 1e-6. The original model has well-scaled optimal points (x_q = 0), so the error is made by the reduction, and it is the tie case of weak domination. With the huge bounds the generator draws (E/tests/oracle.hpp:100, up to 1e22) the term counts as infinite in both activities (E/include/gprs/numerics.hpp:105-108) and the spacing is 2.1e6. The lock rule also fixes at huge bounds (E/src/rules_dual_fixing.cpp:42-58), but there no row needs a compensation. 'An infinite target bound is left alone' covers only IEEE infinity.
defects.fix: R6 fixes only at a value v with |v| * tol.side_error <= tol.feasibility and with no term a * v of the column counted as infinite; otherwise the pair is left and marked (a function of the state, so not 'limited'). The merge already refuses such bounds through its side guard. Add a twin with a huge finite bound to p_parallel_col and a wrong engine that drops the guard.

defects.what: R7 requires down_locks >= 1 and up_locks >= 1 and gives as reason 'a column without a lock in one direction is the lock rule's'. The driver (State and driver, item 5) also puts R8 behind 'with locks both ways', which contradicts R8's own entry. Both exclude a column with cost > 0 that rows lock down only, and the mirror.
defects.why_it_fails: The lock rule acts only when the missing lock is in the cost direction (E/src/rules_dual_fixing.cpp:39-41: cost >= 0 with no down lock, cost <= 0 with no up lock). Model A: min x; x + y >= 3; x integer in [0,10]; y in [0,5]. down_locks[x] = 1, up_locks[x] = 0, cost 1: the lock rule leaves it, R7 skips it, although R7's own argument gives x <= 3 and needs no up lock. Model B: min x; x - 5p >= 0; x in [0,5]; p binary. R8's entry takes it (cost >= 0, one down lock, release at p = 0, force at p = 1, x = 5p), the driver's gate skips it. HiGHS takes both: it counts the cost as a lock (H/presolve/HPresolve.cpp:3773-3785, called at H/presolve/HPresolveDualFixing.cpp:276), so such a column reaches the substitution and the bound strengthening (:333-358). Model B is the standard case of the dual-fixing substitution. No validity is lost; what is lost is an unmeasured part of the 19,965 bound changes and 74,920 substitutions that the M4 prediction (0.9996) assumes our form reaches.
defects.fix: R7: direction down needs cost >= 0 and down_locks >= 1, direction up needs cost <= 0 and up_locks >= 1, nothing about the other direction. Driver: every candidate that is still live after R2 to R5 goes to R7 and R8 whatever its locks; the columns the lock rule fixes are gone by then. Put both models into the unit tests and into p_single_lock.

defects.what: The twin extension of the oracle solver is called exact 'because for a fixed sum the objective is linear in one twin over an interval, so an optimum has one of the two at a bound'. That is true for two continuous twins. It is false when a twin is an integer line column, which the knob allows ('a line-column copy of a line column' with its own bounds; a line column is integer with probability 1 - p_continuous, E/tests/oracle.hpp:98; scales 1, -1, 2, -2).
defects.why_it_fails: Model: x_p continuous in [0,2]; x_q integer in [0,10] (a line column, wider than max_width); one row x_p + 2 x_q = 5. The only points have x_q = 2, x_p = 1. The split fixes x_p = 0 (x_q = 2.5), x_p = 2 (x_q = 1.5), x_q = 0 (x_p = 5), x_q = 10 (x_p = -15): all four cases are infeasible, so the base model is called infeasible. A presolve that wrongly returns infeasible then passes (E/tests/oracle.cpp:939-941) and a right one fails. With scale 1 the same happens on a reduced model once a bound of the continuous twin is fractional: x_p in [0,2.5], x_p + x_q = 5, min -x_p has its optimum at x_p = 2, x_q = 3 with neither twin at a bound, and the split returns x_p = 0. An integer line twin can also stop being a twin in the reduced model, because coefficient strengthening changes its coefficient in one row; into_class then fails a correct result (oracle.cpp:964-966).
defects.fix: Draw line twins as two continuous columns only (any of the four scales), and integer copies only of enumerated columns, which need no split. into_class accepts a pair only when both columns are continuous and proportional in every row. State in oracle.hpp what the split is exact for and why (a vertex of box and strip has a twin at a bound; one twin with two finite bounds, so there is no free direction), and add the model above as a fixed test of the solver.

defects.what: Three wrong engines cannot be caught by the check named for them, and one fixed case does not reach the rule it is for. By the design's own rule ('a wrong engine that is not caught stops the milestone') this stops M1, M2 and M3 or leads to a waiver.
defects.why_it_fails: (a) fs_int (integrality test of R2 dropped) is assigned to 'crush integrality'. For a feasible point x the crushed point does not hold the column and the postsolved value is (b' - g(x))/a = x_k, an integer, so clauses 2 and 3 of E/check/crush_check.hpp:13-18 cannot see it. Only a reduced point that is no crushed point shows it (2 x_k + y = 4, x_k integer in [0,2], y integer in [0,3]: y = 1 gives x_k = 1.5): that is the oracle and the 'integral form' test of the structure check. (b) sp_cont (rounding restriction for a continuous column dropped) is assigned to the oracle. The generator has integer data and scales by powers of two down to 2^-10 (oracle.hpp:103-106), so a gap is 0 or about 1e-3 and more; a gap between rounding size and the forcing tolerance (at most 1e-6) never occurs, and the listed fixed case ('just above the forcing tolerance') is for sp_gap. (c) pd_prop (proportionality tolerance 1e-2) is assigned to the oracle and to crush clause 2: coefficients are integers up to 3 (oracle.hpp:80) and copies are exact multiples, so no generated pair is proportional to 1e-2 and not exactly. (d) The fixed case 2x + 2y = 3 with two integer columns is decided by row tightening in the cascade ('infeasible when an equation gets a fractional right-hand side', E/include/gprs/rules.hpp:171-172) before the column rules run.
defects.fix: fs_int: name the structure check (integral form) and the oracle. sp_cont: a fixed oracle case such as 2p + x1 + x2 = 2 + 2e-7 with x1 continuous in [0,1], x2 integer in [0,1], a cost on p that prefers p = 1 and a second row 1000 x1 >= 1.5e-4; the right engine leaves the row, the wrong one puts x1 = 0 at p = 1 and loses that value of p. pd_prop: replace it by 'one row of the pair is not compared', which integer data show, or add a pair such as (100, 100) against (100, 101). Run 2x + 2y = 3 with the tightening family switched off.

defects.what: pivot_ratio_limit = 1000 bounds one substitution of R2 or R5; substitutions chain and the ratios multiply. The risk note of the design names one link, and 'the bound holds to the tolerance' in R2's postsolve is true only at reduced points that lie exactly inside their bounds.
defects.why_it_fails: r1: x1 + 1000 x2 = 0, x1 a singleton in [-1000, 1000]; r2: x2 + 1000 x3 = 0, x2 in [-1, 1] and only in r1 and r2; x3 in [-1e-3, 1e-3] with other rows. R2 removes x1 with r1 (the range of -1000 x2 is its box, ratio 1000), x2 becomes a singleton and R2 removes it with r2. A reduced point with x3 = 1e-3 + 1e-6, inside the feasibility tolerance, postsolves to x2 = -1.001 and x1 = 1001: bound violations of 1e-3 and 1. The structure check does not see it (it tests points inside the bounds); the check that solves the reduced model with HiGHS does, as a postsolved point that fails.
defects.fix: Keep a factor per column that a substitution multiplies along the chain (the factor of a column in the saved row becomes at least the removed column's factor times the ratio) and test it against one limit, so that the composed ratio and not the single one is bounded; report the largest composed ratio per instance at M2. State what the undo does when the value passes the bound by more than the tolerance.

defects.what: R8 pushes an alias record with row = r although r stays in the model. The record and the check read the row of an alias as a row that leaves the model: E/include/gprs/postsolve.hpp:27-28 ('from the doubleton equation row'), E/check/structure_check.hpp:282 sets row_gone for it, and :301 rejects a later row_addition record that names such a row.
defects.why_it_fails: A lock row that later has an equation subtracted from it, or is subtracted itself, gives the stack error 'rows of row addition record' on a correct result. The lock row is an inequality with a binary and stays a candidate of the parallel rows. The M4 check extension does not mention it.
defects.fix: Give the lock alias no row (row = -1, with push_alias, stack_consistent and postsolve_hash accepting it for origin lock), or let compose_records set row_gone only for the origins doubleton and probing.

defects.what: The undo of a merge is defined only for z inside the merged bounds ('the conditions make the admissible set non-empty').
defects.why_it_fails: A reduced point may use the tolerance. Two continuous columns in [0,1] merged to z in [0,2]: z = 2 + 5e-7 leaves x_removed the set [1 + 5e-7, 1], which is empty, and the closed form has no value. For two integers z is rounded first, but a solver point one step outside the bounds has the same problem.
defects.fix: State the fallback as R3 does: when the admissible interval is empty, x_removed is the point of its own bounds nearest to it and x_kept = z - scale * x_removed, so the excess goes to one column; test it in test_postsolve_records.cpp.

defects.what: Clause 5 of the crush check ('z equals x' in primal-only mode) is kept unchanged until M5, but from M2 on R2 recomputes the removed column from its pivot row.
defects.why_it_fails: A point is used when it misses a row by at most 1e-7 times the largest term (E/check/crush_check.hpp:66, 113-116), and the undo divides that miss by the pivot. Row x_k + 1000 y1 - 1000 y2 = 0 with y1 = 100, y2 = 100.00000001, x_k = 0: the row is off by 1e-5, scaled 1e-10, so the point is used; z_k = 1e-5, the difference is above check_tolerance = 1e-6, the column counts as moved (:431-433) and the round trip fails in primal-only mode (:439) on a correct result. The doubleton alias has the same form today but only two terms of equal size.
defects.fix: From M2 on, for a column removed by a col_from_rows record, compare z with x up to the residual of x in the saved row divided by |a|, or exempt the column and require the saved row to hold at z.

missing: A size rule for the value R6 fixes at, and what R6 does with a bound whose term counts as infinite in an activity (numerics.hpp:105-108); the design treats only IEEE infinity as infinite there.
How the added_rows test and the parallel-row test of the structure check in E read a snapshot and a virtual column; the design covers only a row's own snapshot chain.

Which types and scales the generator draws for line twins, and what into_class does with a twin pair in a reduced model.
