What holds. The one-rule-off numbers reproduce exactly (parallel columns 1.0104, simple probing 1.0103, rule 8 1.0089, rule 17 1.0063, rule 18 1.0012). So does today's position: 0.9563 in nonzeros, 0.9653 in rows, 0.9424 in columns, 39 instances below 0.95, the engine ahead on 9. The reference needs no expensive stage for anything in it, so it is a fair target. It does use three kinds of state the design excludes: implied row-dual bounds, implied bounds of continuous columns in simple probing and bound strengthening, and the implied-integer type. The cost of excluding them is not measured as a whole. Calling each column family once per round does bound the long-column rescans that cost HiGHS its time. I found no oscillation: every rule removes a row or a column, or only tightens. I found no premise without an event.

Where it is wrong.
1. The predicted gate values (0.968, 0.985, 0.994, 0.9996, 1.001) credit 21% of the gap to milestones that no measurement ties it to. With only measured losses credited the values are 0.9661, 0.9827, 0.9913, 0.9973, 0.9988, and without bobin 0.9918 at the end.
2. The bobin chain is not established by any stored run, and its forcing-column half is contradicted by the data.
3. The gate decides on nonzeros alone, while today twelve instances are below 0.95 in rows or columns and above it in nonzeros.
4. R8 scans its lock row once per column, up to 1000 times the nonzeros, on a budget it shares with the O(1) singleton rules, which it can starve.
5. Singleton-column chains cost one round per link against max_rounds = 20.
6. The price of the left-out dual rules (1.0007) is taken from runs in which they replace each other.

The other three are a wrong work bound for R1 and R8, the milestone order, and R8's small separable worth.

defects.what: The predicted gate value of each milestone credits gains that no built rule is measured to deliver. predict.py (stage1c_design/synthesis/predict.py:23-36) sets an instance to the reference size times the one-rule-off losses of the rules not yet built. For an instance that no single switch loses, that product is 1, so the instance counts as closed from M1 on. Only bobin is held back, until M2.
defects.why_it_fails: Recomputed in a1.py and pred2.py. The summed log gap over 237 instances is 10.60, the one-rule-off losses sum to 8.88, and 2.21 (21%) has no single-rule attribution: neos-3402294-bobin 1.660, neos-2746589-doon 0.195, neos-827175 0.088, unitcal_7 0.075, n5-3 0.071, icir97_tension 0.031, binkar10_1 0.018, savsched1 0.014, neos-3627168-kasai 0.012. The model books all of these but bobin at M1, although simple probing fires zero times on each of them in the reference (substitutions.simple_probing = 0 in G/highs_cheap_all/summary.json). The design's own numbers show the error: 0.9563 * 1.0103 = 0.9661, not 0.968. Crediting only measured losses, plus bobin from M2, gives 0.9661, 0.9827, 0.9913, 0.9973, 0.9988, and four instances stay below 0.95 at the end where the design says none (doon 0.82, neos-827175 0.92, unitcal_7 0.93, n5-3 0.93). Without bobin the values are 0.9661, 0.9759, 0.9844, 0.9903, 0.9918. So the M1 acceptance value cannot be met by the rule M1 builds, M3 clears 0.99 by 0.001 and not by 0.004, and the final margin is 0.002 to 0.009 depending on two unmeasured things. Gate item 2 ('explained by a left-out rule with its ablation number') also cannot be decided for these instances, because they have no ablation number.
defects.fix: Measure instead of modelling. Run HiGHS presolve-only on the 240 with exactly the rule set of each milestone switched on: the Stage 1 setting of G/highs_stage1c (presolve_rule_off 9175456 and its switch list), then simple_probing on; then bits 8 and 18 and the 5/23/7 group on; then parallel_columns on; then dual_fixing_substitution on. That is five runs of about 300 s each, which fits the dev node. Use those sizes as the acceptance value of each milestone and as the per-instance target. Until they exist, state M1 as 0.966 and list the nine unattributed instances as open.

defects.what: The design states that the bobin chain is 'R3 and R4, then the lock rule' and books 0.0070 of the 0.0447 mean log gap at M2. No stored run supports this, and the R4 half is contradicted.
defects.why_it_fails: bobin has 381,000 nonzeros in all thirteen ablation files, so neither rule 7 nor rule 18 is necessary there. Its sister instance neos-3402454-bohle has the same 2,904 columns, 132 forcing columns and 132 zero-cost singletons. With rule 7 off, bohle keeps exactly 132 columns and 132 rows more (2,640 and 2,881,360 against 2,508 and 2,881,228). So a missing forcing column is visible on bohle and not on bobin: the forcing columns do not start bobin's 1,848 fixings. Each ablation run also has a substitute path in the HiGHS code. With rule 18 off, the singleton column's only lock is an equation and the single-equation extension is called (H/HPresolveDualFixing.cpp:300-314). With rule 17 off, the dominated-column test takes the fixings (it runs first, H/HPresolve.cpp:2409 and 3536). No stored run has the engine's setting after M2: lock rule only, no rule 23, no extension, rule 18 on. The 1,848 fixings are counted as weakly dominated, a test on implied row-dual bounds (H/HPresolve.cpp:3646-3648), so it is untested whether plain lock counts reach them. My reading of H/HPresolveZeroCostSingleton.cpp:28-52 (an equation with a zero-cost continuous singleton becomes one-sided) makes R3 then the lock rule plausible, but that is inference. Without bobin the gate ends at 0.9918 by measured losses.
defects.fix: Before M2 is detailed, run HiGHS presolve-only on bobin and bohle with the Stage 1 switch set and only bit 18 cleared from presolve_rule_off; this takes seconds. If bobin reaches 381,000, R3 plus the lock rule is confirmed. If not, the chain needs a row-dual bound or the single-equation extension, and M2 is worth 0.0070 less. Take R4 out of the bobin argument. Its evidence is neos-2746589-doon: 112 forcing columns that remove 2,576 rows, a gap of 0.223 of which rule 7 off shows only 0.027.

defects.what: The gate decides on nonzeros only. Rows and columns are 'reported next to it', and the 0.95 floor per instance is on nonzeros.
defects.why_it_fails: From gate.py. Today the engine is at 0.9563 in nonzeros, 0.9653 in rows and 0.9424 in columns, so columns are the weakest measure. Eight instances are at or above 0.95 in nonzeros and below it in columns: roll3000 0.841, neos-3402454-bohle 0.864, physiciansched6-2 0.882, neos-4647030-tutaki 0.889, seymour1 0.911, seymour 0.919, physiciansched3-3 0.930, savsched1 0.943. Four are below it in rows: tutaki 0.800, csched007 0.856, rococoC10-001000 0.943, rococoB10-011000 0.946. On tutaki rule 8 removes 1,400 rows and 1,400 columns that hold 8,400 of 1.98 million nonzeros, so the nonzero ratio is 0.996. By rule, in mean log: rule 18 is 0.0012 in nonzeros and 0.0064 in columns; simple probing 0.0102 and 0.0217; parallel columns 0.0104, 0.0015 in rows and 0.0138 in columns. A weak R3 or R9 would pass this gate. csched007 loses 50 of 347 rows to implied equations, which the design leaves out; in nonzeros it shows as 0.984 and is listed as an acceptable remainder. After M5, by measured losses, columns still have eight instances below 0.95 (pred3.out).
defects.fix: Make all three measures gate values: geometric mean at least 0.99 in nonzeros, in rows and in columns, and the 0.95 floor with the same explanation rule on each. Report matrix nonzeros plus objective nonzeros next to it, because R2 and R5 remove a row by moving its entries into the cost (the design's cost_fill). Decision 3 of the plan names nonzeros only, so this needs the owner's word and belongs in the decision list.

defects.what: R8 scans its lock row, up to 1000 entries, once for every column whose single lock is that row. Its cost entry calls this 'one scan of r of at most 1000 entries' per column.
defects.why_it_fails: The work is the sum over rows of (single-lock columns of the row) times (row length), so up to 1000 times the nonzeros. It is spent on the budget that R2 to R5 and R7 share. Smallest model: 1000 binaries with negative cost, one knapsack row (<=) and one cover row (>=) over all of them. Every column has one up lock, in the knapsack row, and locks both ways. No binary releases the row, so every column scans 1000 entries and finds nothing: 10^6 units on 2,000 nonzeros. A pass is 2000 + 8 * 1002 = 10,016 units (E/include/gprs/presolve.hpp:69-76), so the stall limit of {8, 4, 1e5} is 140,064. The call stops after about 140 columns with no finding (E/include/gprs/rules.hpp:34). A round without a finding ends the rounds (E/src/presolve.cpp:280-284), so the columns behind are never tried by the O(1) rules R2 to R5 either, and the result is no fixed point. With 100 such blocks the call stops after about 4,100 of 100,000 columns. HiGHS has the same scan (H/HPresolveDualFixing.cpp:36, 62) but no budget.
defects.fix: The release test (i) does not depend on x. Compute, once per call for each lock row and locking side, the list of (binary, value) pairs that release it; this is O(row length) and the list is usually empty. A column then pays O(1) plus the force test on that list, and the total is the nonzeros of the lock rows. Recompute the list for a row whose version changed. Also give R8 its own budget or run it after the singleton rules, so that a stall cannot starve them.

defects.what: A chain of singleton columns costs one round per link. The column family visits its candidates 'each once per call, in index order', is called once per round, and max_rounds = 20 counts the rounds of the whole presolve (E/include/gprs/presolve.hpp:97, E/src/presolve.cpp:268).
defects.why_it_fails: Smallest model: free continuous columns x_1..x_T; rows t = 1..T are equations x_(t-1) + x_t + (two other columns) = d_t, with no x_0 in row 1. Only x_T is a singleton. R2 removes x_T and row T, which makes x_(T-1) a singleton, but x_(T-1) was already visited in this call, so it waits for the next round. That gives T rounds. With T = 30 the presolve ends on max_rounds with ten rows and columns left and no fixed point. With the column order reversed the same model is finished in one call, so the result depends on the order. Each extra round also pays a full cascade, parallel rows, doubleton equations and their end_phase calls. HiGHS has no such limit: its singleton list is a work queue that grows while it is processed (H/HPresolve.cpp:4884, fed at :578). In the reference 2,200 of the 16,881 free column substitutions come after the first scan (stage.out): snp-02-004-104 1,224 of 1,556, highschool1-aigio 358 of 359, physiciansched3-3 187 of 194, supportcase42 140 of 140. The counters do not give the chain depth, so how often 20 is reached is unknown. The design's risk note on rounds names the path through the cascade, not this chain inside the family.
defects.fix: Inside one call of column_rules, append a column whose live size drops to 1 through a deletion made by this call to the call's candidates. defects.what: The design leaves out the dominated column by reduced-cost bound (rules 5 and 23) and the single-equation extension, and prices them at 'together about 1.0007' from one-rule-off runs. It asks the owner to change A8 on that number.
defects.why_it_fails: In HiGHS these rules stand in for each other, so each one-rule-off run hides the other's work. savsched1 has 11,615 single-equation fixings and 4,760 bound fixings in the all-on run, yet rule 17 off costs 54 columns and rule 5 off costs nothing (onerule.out). neos-827175 has 732 of its 738 fixings from the single equation, no switch loses anything, and the engine is at 0.916. irish-electricity has 630. In total the extension makes 13,017 fixings on 11 instances and has no switch of its own. The design builds neither rule, has no row-dual state, and says of R7 that 'the clip never acts through' an equation. So no built rule sees through an equation that is a column's only lock, unless a zero-cost singleton slack is there for R3. No stored run has both rules off with bound strengthening on. The price of leaving out both is therefore unmeasured, and savsched1 at 0.943 in columns is the visible candidate. defects.what: The work bound of R1, and by the shared code of R8, is wrong: 'A column is substituted once, so the total over the presolve is at most the nonzeros.'
defects.why_it_fails: A column is substituted once, but the binary inherits its entries and can itself be substituted later, which moves them again. Smallest model: binaries, rows k = 1..n with x_k + y_k - 2 x_(k+1) = 0, and x_1 in L further rows. In index order, row k substitutes x_k by x_(k+1) and moves the L inherited entries each time. That is n * L moves on about 3n + L nonzeros; with n = L = 10^4 it is 10^8 moves on 4 * 10^4 nonzeros. The budget {4, 2, 1e5} then stops the call every round and the chain is not finished in 20 rounds. In reverse row order each column moves once. The doubleton family avoids this by collecting a batch in the alias forest and substituting each column once into its root (E/src/rules_doubleton.cpp:191-243). The design takes that family's substitute() but not its batch. HiGHS substitutes at once as the design does, so this concerns our own bound, and the chain depth on real instances is not known.
defects.fix: Collect the aliases of the listed rows of a call first, compose them (a column whose binary is itself aliased in the same call goes straight to the final binary), then substitute once per column. Otherwise state the bound as nonzeros times alias depth and report the depth at M1 on highschool1-aigio, brazil3 and neos-1445765.
